name: Vesper Tuivailala-Esquivel
location: The Stockyard, Pier 4 overflow lot, Grainfort, near Lake Shore and Navy Pier
description:
Vashti is lean and angular with the kind of wiry strength that comes from hauling scrap rather than any intentional exercise. Their skin is a deep warm brown, and they have geneware cat ears — dusty grey tabby-patterned, which they've never bothered to remove since getting them at nineteen on a dare — that flatten expressively when they're annoyed and perk forward when something catches their interest, which is often. A bioluminescent stripe runs down the back of each forearm, dim pale blue, activated by stress hormones; they've learned to read it as an early warning system for their own anxiety. Their work clothes are pragmatic catastrophes: safety-orange strapping over layered thermals, magnetic tool clips everywhere, boots with steel inserts they sourced from a Ferrogate Transit maintenance surplus sale.

They have the paradoxical quality of seeming both completely at ease in the chaos of the Stockyard lots and perpetually slightly amused by it, as though the entire enterprise of human commerce is a joke they're in on. Their actual eye for value is extraordinary — they can assess a pile of mixed scrap and name a fair price in under thirty seconds, and they're almost never wrong. They're known for being the only merchant in Grainfort who won't claim something works if it doesn't.

core_fears: Being trapped in a role or place with no room to manoeuvre
Trusting someone who uses that trust as leverage
core_desires: Enough financial cushion to walk away from a bad situation
Work that feels honest — no pretending something is what it isn't
coping_mechanisms: Physical work — sorting and cataloguing to quiet the mind
Reading the bioluminescent stripes as a biofeedback tool
blind_spots: Their comfort with chaos means they sometimes miss when a situation has become genuinely dangerous rather than just messy
psychology.secret: They've been documenting serial numbers on certain Ferrogate Transit parts coming through the Stockyard — parts that shouldn't exist on the secondary market. They don't know yet what they're going to do with the information, but the file is growing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Casual, technically precise about anything mechanical, fond of dry asides; code-switches between Yoruba proverbs (from their grandmother) and Czech slang (from their father's neighbourhood) without noticing
speech_patterns.cadence: Easy and unhurried, with sudden bursts of rapid technical detail when something gets interesting
verbal_tics: 'Honestly?' as a sentence opener for honest assessments
example_lines: Honestly? This actuator is cooked. I'll take it off you for Φ4 and strip the housing, which is actually fine. Offering you Φ4 for a dead actuator is me being charitable.
My baba used to say — well, he'd say it in Czech and I'd understand maybe half — something about how everything valuable is just something someone else stopped paying attention to. Seems right to me.

story_hooks: The Ferrogate Transit serial number file becomes dangerous when one of the maintenance workers figures out Vashti has been documenting
A specific piece of scrap comes through the lot that is clearly not junk — it's a piece of something that should not exist on the open market at all, and the person who sold it is already dead
narrative_function: Scrap and salvage information source — knows what's being thrown away by whom; can source unusual components; potential lead on Ferrogate Transit's internal disposal practices; local colour with genuine warmth.
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (grey tabby, cosmetic). Bioluminescent stripes on forearms (geneware, stress-reactive). Subdermal magnetic fingertips (functional — allows them to handle small metal components without dropping them).
daily_life: Early morning scavenging runs to the Grainfort overflow before other pickers arrive, then sorting and pricing through midday, then open stall from noon to whenever the light goes.
affiliation: Independent; trade relationship with three Ferrogate Transit maintenance workers who sell surplus parts off-manifest; loosely pays protection to the Stockyard crew

decision_rules: Don't lie about what something is — your reputation is the business
Keep one exit always mentally mapped
escalation_ladder: Walking away entirely — no scene, no argument, just gone

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Cheerfully professional and slightly guarded — warm but watching
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed, generous, teasing; will help quietly without making it a thing

stress_responses.low: Gets more talkative and jokes more
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet, watches the bioluminescent stripes, starts tidying the stall
stress_responses.high: Leaves. Just leaves. Comes back when it's done.

contradictions: Values honesty above almost everything but is sitting on information that could burn several people
habits: Runs magnetic fingertips along metal surfaces when idle
Cat ears flatten when reading the bioluminescent stripes — focuses inward
breaking_points: Being deliberately deceived by someone they'd decided to trust

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American with South Asian, Pacific Islander, and Southeast Asian ancestry; warm golden-brown complexion with subtle olive undertones from the regional blend
physical_description.build: Lean and angular with wiry muscle definition from years of hauling scrap; no excess body fat; sinewy forearms and core strength despite slight frame
physical_description.hair_style: Worn in loose twists, often half-pinned back with salvaged metal clips to keep it clear of work
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with subtle olive undertones; sun-weathered on shoulders and neck from outdoor scrap work
physical_description.complexion: Balanced facial geometry with defined cheekbones reflecting South Asian and Hispanic heritage; warm-toned skin with minor scars and calluses from scrap work; sharp, alert expression
distinguishing_marks: Geneware cat ears mounted at the crown, grey tabby-patterned feline ears with natural musculature allowing independent movement and flattening when annoyed
Pale blue bioluminescent stripes running the length of each forearm on the dorsal side, faintly glowing during moments of stress or heightened adrenaline
Minor burn scarring on the heel of left hand from an early scrap-sorting accident, now barely visible
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware cat ears (cosmetic, animalistic). Bioluminescent forearm stripes (visible as faint pale-blue lines, glow activated by stress). Subdermal magnetic fingertips not visually obvious at rest but create subtle metallic shine under certain light; occasionally small metal shavings cling to fingertips.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision; stands with weight shifted to one side in relaxed stance, often picking up and rotating small objects absently. Cat ears track sounds and movement with subtle autonomic twitches. Overall demeanor is alert but unbothered, moving through chaos with practiced ease.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class pragmatism: safety-orange high-visibility strapping harness worn over layered thermal undershirts in grey or black. Multiple magnetic tool clips on webbing. Reinforced cargo pants with patched seams, tucked into steel-insert work boots sourced from Ferrogate Transit surplus. Occasional technical jacket in faded blue or neutral tones when weather demands. No visible corporate branding; all gear is salvaged or secondhand. Grooming is minimal but deliberate — nothing wasted, everything functional.
